name: Data and AI leadership vocabulary
description: The 100 terms a technology leader needs for data strategy, platforms, analytics, machine learning, generative AI, governance and privacy.

cards.subject: data strategy
says: sets out how an organisation will collect, manage and use data to meet its goals
links data work to business outcomes
cards.use: are asked how data investment will support the company's goals
not: is a list of the databases currently in use

cards.subject: data product
says: is a dataset or service managed like a product, with an owner, users and quality standards
is built to be reused by other teams
cards.use: want a team to publish a trusted customer dataset that others can rely on
not: is any file saved on a shared drive

cards.subject: data mesh
says: gives each business domain ownership of its own data as products
shares common standards across domains instead of using one central team
cards.use: find that a central data team is a bottleneck for every business area
not: puts all data into one central store managed by one team

cards.subject: data catalogue
says: is a searchable inventory of an organisation's data with descriptions and owners
helps people find and understand data
cards.use: hear analysts say they cannot tell which dataset to trust
not: stores the data itself

cards.subject: data lineage
says: records where data came from and how it was changed on the way
lets people trace a number back to its source
cards.use: are asked why a figure in a board report differs from last month's
not: is the order in which files were saved

cards.subject: master data management
says: keeps one agreed record of core entities such as customers and products
removes conflicting versions held in different systems
cards.use: find the same customer recorded differently in sales, billing and support
not: is a backup of the main database

cards.subject: single source of truth
says: is one agreed place where a given piece of data is held and trusted
stops teams from using conflicting copies
cards.use: see two departments reporting different revenue totals from separate spreadsheets
not: means that a single person owns all the data

cards.subject: data owner
says: is the accountable person for a dataset and decisions about its use
decides who may access the data
cards.use: need a named person to approve access to payroll data
not: writes the daily scripts that move the data

cards.subject: data steward
says: looks after the quality, definitions and day-to-day rules of a dataset
works within the policy set by the owner
cards.use: need someone to keep the definitions and quality of customer data consistent
not: is accountable for approving access at the senior level

cards.subject: data literacy
says: is the ability to read, question and use data and charts sensibly
can be built across a whole organisation
cards.use: want managers to understand and challenge the numbers in reports
not: is the skill of building data pipelines

cards.subject: data lakehouse
says: combines low-cost lake storage with warehouse-style management and queries
serves analytics and machine learning from one platform
cards.use: want one platform for both reporting and data science
not: is a building that houses servers

cards.subject: ETL
says: extracts data, transforms it, then loads it into a target store
cleans data before it reaches the destination
cards.use: need to reshape data from a source system before it goes into the warehouse
not: loads raw data first and transforms it later inside the target

cards.subject: ELT
says: loads raw data into the target first and transforms it there
uses the processing power of the destination platform
cards.use: want to land raw data quickly and shape it later in the warehouse
not: transforms data before loading it

cards.subject: data pipeline
says: is an automated series of steps that moves and prepares data
runs on a schedule or in response to events
cards.use: need data from several systems to arrive in the warehouse every night
not: is a physical cable between servers

cards.subject: batch processing
says: handles data in large groups at set times
suits work that does not need an instant result
cards.use: produce a report overnight from the whole day's transactions
not: handles each event as soon as it occurs

cards.subject: stream processing
says: handles data continuously as events arrive
supports near-real-time reactions
cards.use: must flag a suspicious card payment within seconds
not: waits and processes a day's data in one run

cards.subject: change data capture
says: detects changes made in a source database and passes them on
avoids copying the whole table each time
cards.use: want the warehouse to reflect changes in the live system without full reloads
not: restores a database from a backup

cards.subject: schema on read
says: applies structure to data when it is queried, not when it is stored
suits raw data in lakes
cards.use: store raw files first and decide how to interpret them later
not: forces data into a fixed structure before it can be saved

cards.subject: data mart
says: is a smaller store of data focused on one business area
draws from a wider warehouse
cards.use: want finance to have its own curated set of tables for reporting
not: is the central store that holds all company data

cards.subject: orchestration
says: schedules and coordinates the steps in data workflows
handles order, retries and dependencies
cards.use: need many data jobs to run in the right order and rerun if one fails
not: is the design of a database table

cards.subject: business intelligence
says: turns data into reports and dashboards that support decisions
focuses on describing what has happened
cards.use: want weekly sales and stock reports available to managers
not: builds predictive models from raw data

cards.subject: self-service analytics
says: lets business users explore data themselves without needing a data specialist
relies on trusted, well-described data
cards.use: want managers to answer routine questions without waiting for a report
not: means every employee builds their own data pipeline

cards.subject: cohort analysis
says: compares groups of users who share a starting point over time
shows how behaviour changes as a group ages
cards.use: want to see how customers who joined in the same month keep returning
not: compares all users in one single average

cards.subject: A/B test
says: compares two versions by showing each to a different, similar group
measures which version performs better
cards.use: want to know whether a new checkout page raises sales
not: asks a single group to rank two designs verbally

cards.subject: correlation versus causation
says: warns that two things moving together does not mean one causes the other
needs controlled evidence to show a cause
cards.use: see ice cream sales and sunburn rising together and are asked what causes what
not: says that correlated things always share a cause

cards.subject: sampling bias
says: occurs when the group studied does not represent the whole population
makes results misleading
cards.use: survey only customers who contact support and draw conclusions about all customers
not: is a mistake in arithmetic during a calculation

cards.subject: data storytelling
says: presents data as a clear narrative with a point and a recommendation
combines charts, context and a message
cards.use: must explain quarterly results to executives so they act on them
not: is the writing of fiction using real names

cards.subject: semantic layer
says: defines business terms and measures once so every tool uses the same meaning
stops different dashboards computing 'revenue' differently
cards.use: find that two dashboards show different figures for the same measure
not: is the storage hardware under the database

cards.subject: supervised learning
says: trains a model on examples that have known answers
learns to predict the label for new cases
cards.use: want a model to predict whether a loan will default using past outcomes
not: finds patterns in data that has no labels

cards.subject: unsupervised learning
says: finds patterns in data without labelled answers
is used for tasks such as grouping similar customers
cards.use: want to discover natural groups of customers with no preset categories
not: learns from examples labelled with the right answer

cards.subject: reinforcement learning
says: learns by trying actions and receiving rewards or penalties
improves its choices through trial and error
cards.use: want a system to learn the best moves through repeated play
not: needs a labelled answer for every example

cards.subject: training data
says: is the set of examples a model learns from
shapes what the model can and cannot do
cards.use: are told a model works poorly because it learned from unrepresentative examples
not: is the data used only to give the final grade of the model

cards.subject: test set
says: is data held back to check how well a model works on unseen cases
is not used during training
cards.use: want an honest measure of how a trained model will perform
not: is the data the model learns from

cards.subject: overfitting
says: is when a model fits its training data too closely and does poorly on new data
learns noise as if it were a pattern
cards.use: see excellent results on training data but poor ones in real use
not: is when a model is too simple to learn any pattern

cards.subject: underfitting
says: is when a model is too simple to capture the pattern in the data
does poorly on both training and new data
cards.use: find a model that scores badly even on the data it was trained on
not: is when a model memorises its training examples

cards.subject: feature engineering
says: creates or transforms input variables to help a model learn
uses knowledge of the problem to shape the data
cards.use: turn a timestamp into day of week to help predict demand
not: is the selection of hardware to run a model

cards.subject: precision and recall
says: measure how many flagged cases are correct and how many true cases are found
trade off against each other
cards.use: are choosing how a fraud model should balance missed fraud against false alarms
not: both measure only how fast a model runs

cards.subject: baseline model
says: is a simple reference model used to judge whether a complex one is worth it
sets the bar a new model must beat
cards.use: want to know whether a costly model really improves on a simple rule
not: is the final model released to customers

cards.subject: MLOps
says: applies engineering and operations practice to build, deploy and run models reliably
covers testing, release and monitoring of models
cards.use: want models moved from a notebook into dependable production use
not: is the study of statistics used in models

cards.subject: model registry
says: stores versions of models with their details and status
records which version is in production
cards.use: need to know which model version is live and who approved it
not: is a list of the users who may query a model

cards.subject: feature store
says: holds shared, reusable input features for training and serving
keeps training and live features consistent
cards.use: want teams to reuse the same customer features without rebuilding them
not: is the place where finished models are stored

cards.subject: model monitoring
says: tracks a deployed model's inputs, outputs and accuracy over time
raises an alert when behaviour changes
cards.use: need to know when a live model starts giving worse results
not: checks the model only once before release

cards.subject: data drift
says: is a change in the data a model sees compared with the data it was trained on
can reduce accuracy without any code change
cards.use: see customer behaviour shift so live inputs differ from the training data
not: is data being lost during a transfer

cards.subject: shadow deployment
says: runs a new model on live traffic without acting on its results
lets its output be compared with the current model
cards.use: want to see how a new model behaves on real requests without risking customers
not: sends all users to the new model at once

cards.subject: champion-challenger
says: runs a proposed model against the current best one on the same task
replaces the current model only if the challenger does better
cards.use: want a controlled contest between the live model and a new candidate
not: retires the older model before testing the new one

cards.subject: model card
says: documents a model's purpose, data, limits and tested performance
helps users judge whether it is suitable
cards.use: need a short document explaining what a model is for and where it should not be used
not: is a card that gives physical access to a data centre

cards.subject: inference
says: is using a trained model to make predictions on new data
happens after training is complete
cards.use: send a new customer's details to a model and get a score back
not: is the process of teaching a model

cards.subject: retraining
says: updates a model with fresher data to restore or improve its accuracy
may be scheduled or triggered by monitoring
cards.use: find that accuracy has fallen because the world changed since the model was built
not: means rewriting the model's code from scratch every release

cards.subject: foundation model
says: is a large model trained on broad data that can be adapted to many tasks
serves as a base for further tuning
cards.use: want one general model that many teams can adapt for different uses
not: is a model trained for a single narrow task only

cards.subject: prompt engineering
says: is crafting the input to a model to get better output
uses clear instructions, context and examples
cards.use: improve answers from a language model by rewording the question
not: is the retraining of the model's weights

cards.subject: fine-tuning
says: continues training a model on specific data to specialise it
changes the model's weights
cards.use: want a model to follow your organisation's style and terminology consistently
not: only changes the wording of the question sent to the model

cards.subject: embedding
says: turns text or other content into a list of numbers that capture its meaning
places similar items close together
cards.use: want to find documents that mean the same as a question even if the words differ
not: is a model's final written answer

cards.subject: vector database
says: stores embeddings and finds the closest matches quickly
supports search by meaning
cards.use: need to retrieve the most similar passages to a question
not: is a database for storing drawing files only

cards.subject: context window
says: is the amount of text a model can consider at one time
includes both the input and the output
cards.use: find that a long document does not fit into one request
not: is the time a model takes to answer

cards.subject: token
says: is a small piece of text that a language model reads and writes
is a unit for measuring length and usage
cards.use: want to understand how the length of a prompt is measured
not: is a physical security device used to log in

cards.subject: AI agent
says: uses a model to decide on and carry out steps, often calling tools
works towards a goal over several steps
cards.use: want a system that plans a task and calls tools such as search or a database
not: is a person who represents a company in contract talks

cards.subject: guardrails
says: are controls that limit what an AI system will accept or produce
can block unsafe, off-topic or private content
cards.use: want to stop a chatbot answering outside its allowed scope
not: are the physical barriers in a data centre

cards.subject: grounding
says: ties a model's answers to trusted sources supplied with the request
reduces the chance of invented answers
cards.use: want a model to answer only from your approved policy documents
not: is the earthing of electrical equipment

cards.subject: responsible AI
says: is designing and using AI in line with principles such as fairness and accountability
covers the whole lifecycle of a system
cards.use: are asked how the company will make sure its AI is used safely and fairly
not: is any AI system that has passed its tests

cards.subject: algorithmic bias
says: is systematic unfairness in a system's results for some groups
often stems from skewed data or design choices
cards.use: find a hiring model that scores one group of applicants lower for no good reason
not: is a random error that affects all people equally

cards.subject: explainability
says: is the ability to give understandable reasons for a model's output
helps people challenge and trust a decision
cards.use: must tell a customer why an application was declined by a model
not: is the speed at which a model returns an answer

cards.subject: AI impact assessment
says: examines the possible harms and benefits of an AI system before it is used
is done early and revisited as the system changes
cards.use: are about to deploy a model that affects customers' access to a service
not: is a test of a model's speed under load

cards.subject: model risk management
says: controls the risks that come from errors or misuse of models
includes validation, limits and ongoing review
cards.use: must show regulators that models used in decisions are validated and monitored
not: is the insurance purchased against server failures

cards.subject: AI usage policy
says: sets out what staff may and may not do with AI tools
covers matters such as confidential data and review of outputs
cards.use: find staff pasting customer data into public chatbots
not: lists the models a company has trained

cards.subject: human oversight
says: keeps a person able to review, override or stop an automated decision
is stronger where the effects on people are serious
cards.use: want a person to check the system's decisions before they affect customers
not: means a person writes every decision by hand

cards.subject: automated decision-making
says: is deciding about people using only automated processing
can have specific legal limits and rights
cards.use: use a system that approves or rejects loans with no person involved
not: is the use of a calculator in a meeting

cards.subject: AI red teaming
says: tests an AI system by deliberately trying to make it fail or misbehave
looks for harmful or unsafe outputs
cards.use: want to find ways a chatbot could be pushed into unsafe answers before release
not: is a plan to buy red-coloured hardware

cards.subject: fairness metric
says: is a measure used to compare a model's outcomes across groups
different measures can conflict with one another
cards.use: want to check whether error rates are similar between groups
not: is a measure of how quickly a model trains

cards.subject: personal data
says: is information that relates to an identifiable living person
includes names, identifiers and online data
cards.use: must decide whether a dataset falls under privacy law
not: is any information stored on a computer

cards.subject: special category data
says: is a more sensitive kind of personal data, such as health or ethnicity
needs extra protection and a further condition for use
cards.use: are asked to process staff health records
not: is any data stored in a special database

cards.subject: lawful basis
says: is the legal reason that allows personal data to be used
must be identified before the processing starts
cards.use: want to know what permits you to process customer data for a service
not: is the chosen method for encrypting data

cards.subject: consent
says: is a person's free, specific and informed agreement to the use of their data
can be withdrawn
cards.use: ask users to opt in to marketing messages
not: is the same as a data processing agreement

cards.subject: data subject access request
says: is a person's request to see the personal data held about them
must be answered within a set time
cards.use: receive a letter from a customer asking for a copy of all data you hold on them
not: is a request to delete the company's whole database

cards.subject: data minimisation
says: means collecting only the personal data that is needed for the purpose
reduces risk by holding less
cards.use: are about to add an optional birth date field that nothing uses
not: means storing as much data as possible for later

cards.subject: pseudonymisation
says: replaces identifying details with a code, with the key held separately
still counts as personal data
cards.use: want analysts to work on records without seeing names but keep the ability to link back
not: permanently removes any way to identify a person

cards.subject: anonymisation
says: removes identifying details so a person can no longer be identified
makes data fall outside personal data rules when done properly
cards.use: want to publish statistics that cannot be traced to anyone
not: replaces names with codes that can be reversed with a key

cards.subject: data retention
says: sets how long data is kept before it is deleted
is based on legal and business need
cards.use: must decide how many years to keep old customer records
not: is the backup of data kept in case of loss

cards.subject: privacy by design
says: builds data protection into a system from the start
treats privacy as a default and not an add-on
cards.use: are starting a new product and want to include privacy from the first design
not: adds privacy controls only after a breach

cards.subject: data masking
says: hides sensitive values in a copy of data by replacing them with realistic substitutes
lets teams test without real personal data
cards.use: want developers to test with data that looks real but contains no genuine customers
not: permanently deletes a dataset

cards.subject: tokenisation
says: replaces a sensitive value with a token that has no usable meaning
keeps the original in a separate secure vault
cards.use: want to store a payment card reference without holding the real number
not: scrambles data with a key that can reverse it everywhere

cards.subject: encryption at rest
says: protects stored data by encrypting it on the disk or in the database
guards against theft of the storage
cards.use: want a stolen disk to be unreadable
not: protects data only while it travels across a network

cards.subject: encryption in transit
says: protects data while it moves between systems
guards against interception
cards.use: want data sent across a network to be unreadable to anyone listening
not: protects data only while it sits on a disk

cards.subject: data loss prevention
says: detects and blocks sensitive data from leaving the organisation
can scan email, uploads and devices
cards.use: want to stop employees emailing customer lists to personal accounts
not: is the process of restoring deleted files

cards.subject: data sharing agreement
says: is a document that sets out how data will be shared between parties
covers purpose, safeguards and responsibilities
cards.use: are about to pass customer data to a partner organisation
not: is a licence to use software

cards.subject: data clean room
says: lets parties analyse combined data without seeing each other's raw records
returns only agreed, aggregated results
cards.use: want two companies to measure shared customers without exchanging their customer lists
not: is a room with controlled air quality for servers

cards.subject: row-level security
says: limits which rows of a table each user can see
applies the same rule inside the data layer
cards.use: want regional managers to see only their own region's records in one shared table
not: encrypts the whole database file

cards.subject: differential privacy
says: adds carefully measured noise so individuals cannot be picked out of results
protects people while keeping group patterns
cards.use: want to publish statistics and make sure no single person can be identified
not: removes all personal data from the original database

cards.subject: synthetic data
says: is artificially generated data that mimics the patterns of real data
can reduce use of real personal data
cards.use: need realistic data for testing without using real customers
not: is real data copied to a second server

cards.subject: chief data officer
says: is the executive accountable for how an organisation manages and uses its data
sets data strategy and standards
cards.use: want a single executive voice for data across the business
not: runs the daily operation of the servers

cards.subject: data scientist
says: builds statistical and machine learning models to answer questions and make predictions
explores data to find insight
cards.use: need a specialist to build a model that predicts customer churn
not: mainly builds and maintains the production pipelines

cards.subject: data engineer
says: builds and maintains the pipelines and platforms that deliver data
makes data reliable and available
cards.use: need someone to make sure data arrives clean and on time
not: mainly builds models to make predictions

cards.subject: analytics engineer
says: turns raw data into clean, tested models that analysts use
sits between data engineering and analysis
cards.use: want well-defined, tested tables for analysts to build reports on
not: is the person who designs servers in a data centre

cards.subject: ML engineer
says: builds the systems that run machine learning models in production
focuses on reliability and scale
cards.use: need a model to run reliably for thousands of users
not: is a person who only chooses the training examples

cards.subject: AI strategy
says: sets how an organisation will use AI to create value and manage risk
chooses where AI is and is not appropriate
cards.use: are asked where the company should and should not use AI
not: is a list of the AI tools staff have installed

cards.subject: use case prioritisation
says: ranks possible AI or data projects by value, feasibility and risk
decides what is worth building first
cards.use: have thirty AI ideas and budget for three
not: is the order in which servers are installed

cards.subject: pilot purgatory
says: is when many pilots run but few ever reach production
wastes effort without delivering value
cards.use: find that many AI experiments are launched but none reach real users
not: is a place where finished models are stored

cards.subject: data maturity model
says: describes stages by which an organisation's data capability grows
helps set a roadmap of improvements
cards.use: want to see how the organisation's data practice compares with a path to better
not: is a scoring of the age of a company's databases

cards.subject: AI literacy
says: is understanding what AI can and cannot do and how to use it responsibly
can be built across an organisation
cards.use: want staff to understand the limits of AI tools before relying on them
not: is the ability to write code for a model

cards.subject: classification
says: predicts which category an item belongs to
gives answers such as spam or not spam
cards.use: want a model to decide whether each email is spam
not: predicts a number on a continuous scale

qa.q: Analysts say they cannot tell which dataset to trust. What helps first?
qa.right: A data catalogue with owners and descriptions
qa.why: A catalogue shows what data exists, who owns it and what it means.

qa.q: Which role approves access to a payroll dataset?
qa.why: The owner is accountable for decisions about use.

qa.q: What is inference in machine learning?
qa.right: Using a trained model to make predictions on new data
qa.why: Inference is the use of a finished model.

qa.q: You want to compare two web page designs on real visitors. What do you run?
qa.why: Each version is shown to a similar group.

qa.q: What does a data pipeline do?
wrong: Stores a copy of the screen
qa.why: A pipeline automates the movement of data.

qa.q: A team pastes customer data into a public chatbot. Which document should have prevented it?
qa.why: The policy states what staff may do with AI tools.

qa.q: Two dashboards show different totals for revenue. What fixes this in the long term?
qa.right: A semantic layer that defines revenue once
qa.why: A shared definition keeps every tool consistent.

qa.q: A board figure differs from last month's and nobody can say why. What helps trace it?
qa.why: Lineage shows where data came from and what changed.

qa.q: A model scores well on its training data and poorly in real use. What is the likely cause?
qa.why: It learned noise in the training set.

qa.q: You want a model to answer only from your approved policy documents. Which technique helps?
qa.right: Grounding the answers in those documents
qa.why: Grounding ties answers to trusted sources.

qa.q: A model has been live for months and its accuracy has quietly fallen. What should have caught this?
qa.why: Monitoring tracks live behaviour and alerts on changes.

qa.q: Staff must know what a model is for and where it should not be used. What do you write?
qa.why: A model card documents purpose, data and limits.

qa.q: A customer asks for a copy of every piece of data you hold on them. What is this?
qa.why: People may ask to see their personal data.

qa.q: You are about to add an optional birth date field that nothing will use. Which principle applies?
qa.why: Collect only what is needed for the purpose.

qa.q: You need to load raw data fast and reshape it later in the warehouse. Which approach?
qa.why: ELT loads first and transforms inside the target.

qa.q: A card payment must be flagged within seconds. Which processing fits?
qa.why: Streaming handles events as they arrive.

qa.q: A correlation between two measures is shown to the board as proof of cause. What do you say?
qa.right: Correlation does not show cause without controlled evidence
qa.why: Things can move together for other reasons.

qa.q: A central data team is a bottleneck for every business area. Which approach gives domains ownership?
qa.why: A mesh makes domains owners of their data products.

qa.q: A tiny difference in an A/B test with a huge sample is statistically significant. What should you conclude?
qa.right: It is unlikely to be chance, but it may not matter in practice
wrong: The change is worth a large investment
The sample is too big to trust
The test must be rerun with a smaller sample
qa.why: Significance is not the same as importance.

qa.q: A survey only reaches customers who contact support. What is the risk?
qa.why: The sample does not represent all customers.

qa.q: You want to test a new model on live requests without any customer seeing its output. What do you use?
qa.why: Its output is recorded but not acted upon.

qa.q: Analysts can work on records without seeing names, yet you can link them back. What is this?
qa.why: The key is held separately, so the data is still personal.

qa.q: You want to publish statistics that can never be traced to anyone. What is the aim?
qa.why: Properly anonymised data cannot identify people.

qa.q: A fraud model should miss as little fraud as possible, accepting more false alarms. Which measure does this favour?
qa.why: Recall measures how many true cases are found.

qa.q: A model's inputs have shifted away from the data it was trained on. What is this?
qa.why: The live data no longer resembles the training data.

qa.q: You must explain to a customer why a model declined their application. Which property is needed?
qa.why: People need understandable reasons.

qa.q: Regional managers should only see their own region's rows in one shared table. What do you use?
qa.why: The data layer restricts rows by user.

qa.q: You want realistic test data without any real customers. Which approaches fit?
wrong: A copy of the live database
A public dataset of other firms' customers
qa.why: Both avoid exposing real personal data.

qa.q: You have thirty AI ideas and budget for three. Which activity decides?
qa.right: Use case prioritisation by value, feasibility and risk
qa.why: Ranking decides the order.

qa.q: A hiring model gives one group lower scores for no good reason. What is this?
qa.why: The results are systematically unfair to a group.

qa.q: Many AI pilots start but none reach real users. What is the problem?
qa.why: Experiments never become production services.

qa.q: Two companies want to measure shared customers without swapping customer lists. What fits?
qa.why: Only agreed, aggregated results are returned.

qa.q: You want to publish figures while ensuring no individual can be picked out. Which technique adds noise to protect people?
qa.why: Measured noise protects individuals while keeping patterns.

qa.q: You want a controlled contest between the live model and a new candidate on the same task. What do you set up?
qa.why: The challenger replaces the champion only if it does better.

qa.q: A bank is told two fairness measures cannot both be satisfied at once. What is your best response?
qa.right: Choose which fairness measure matters and record why
qa.why: Different fairness measures can conflict, so a documented decision is needed.

qa.q: An executive asks you to deploy an AI model that makes loan decisions with no person involved. What should you check first?
qa.right: Legal limits on automated decision-making and the need for human oversight
wrong: How many tokens the model uses
qa.why: Such decisions about people can have specific legal limits.

qa.q: A model must be tested for harmful outputs before release. Which practice is this?
qa.why: Testers deliberately try to make it misbehave.

qa.q: You want a set of gates that proves a new AI system is safe, lawful and valuable before launch. What do you create?
qa.right: An AI impact assessment and approval process
qa.why: An assessment looks at harms and benefits before use.

qa.q: A company holds the same customer in sales, billing and support under different spellings. What should you build?
qa.right: A master data record for customers
qa.why: Master data management keeps one agreed record.

qa.q: You want models to be reproducible and traceable from data to release. Which combination helps?
qa.right: A model registry and data lineage
qa.why: They record which data and version produced each release.
